title: Resolve path components through kernel, not lexically, except final component
context: lexicalDeepestContainer compared absolute paths using plain path.resolve()/relative(), trusting the false theory that POSIX cancels ".." against the lexically preceding component. The kernel actually cancels ".." against the parent of the current lookup directory—which after a symlink traversal is the target's parent, not its lexical parent. This created false positives (symlinked dirs wrongly attributed) and false negatives (symlink+".." paths wrongly unattributed) whenever ".." followed a symlink. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Always resolve every path component except the final one through the kernel (canonicalRootPath on dirname) before comparison; reattach the raw basename afterward. This preserves the function's original purpose (final component never followed through symlinks) while aligning ".." handling with actual kernel behavior.
consequences: Fixes both false-positive and false-negative mispaths for symlink+".." sequences
Adds a system call (canonicalRootPath/realpathSync.native) per path check—performance cost accepted for correctness
Tests now have non-vacuous adversarial cases that actually exercise kernel symlink behavior, replacing vacuous tests that silently passed before the fix
alternatives_rejected: Pure lexical comparison via path.resolve/relative (original approach; false theory about POSIX cancellation)
Blanket disqualification of any path containing ".." (round 9; refused harmless input on all tools)
Trusting path module output to model kernel behavior without calling through to realpath/native calls
